previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mrs. ___ was admitted with nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain, found to be in acute liver and anuric renal failure with altered mental status requiring intubation and dialysis. She had multifocal pneumonia, likely aspiration-related, treated with vancomycin and Zosyn. Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response was managed with diltiazem, metoprolol, and digoxin. Her liver injury improved without a definitive cause identified. She required mechanical ventilation twice but was successfully extubated and weaned. A tunneled dialysis line was placed after infection of the temporary catheter. Her mental status improved with narcotic reduction. She was discharged to extended care still requiring dialysis, with follow-up planned for cardiology, nephrology, vascular, and liver services.

Brief Hospital Course:
This is a ___ year old female with an extensive past medical 
history significant for stage II breast CA s/p lumpectomy, XRT, 
and ___, Lung SCC stage IA s/p resection in ___: Tracheal 
cancer diagnosed in ___ s/p radiation/chemo, 
fibromyalgia/chronic pain syndrome, a-fib, htn, cad, GERD, COPD, 
and recent hospitalization in MICU for liver and anuric renal 
failure requiring HD (now resolved, but has CKD), HCAP, and 
altered mental status, now presenting with worsening wheezing 
and sputum production likely from COPD exacerbation and CHF 
exacerbation. 

# Dyspnea/wheezing: Upon admission the patient had a wet cough 
and, audible wheezing, and marked airway secretions. She was 
afebrile with a CXR unchanged from her last admission and no 
white count. It was determined that the cause of her symptoms 
was likely due to a combination of COPD exacerbation and CHF 
exacerbation. She was breathing comfortably and satting 99-100% 
on 2L of NC. Her ABG on the night of admission showed reasonable 
ventilation (7.44/48/170/34). For COPD exacerbation she was 
treated with 60mg of prednisone daily, as well as albuterol and 
ipratropium nebs. For CHF she was given lasix at twice her daily 
dose for 2 days until her Na began to drop and her Cr began to 
rise. Following these treatments she showed good symptomatic 
improvement. She had a neck/chest CT that did not show any 
evidence of tracheal obstruction or recurrence of her tracheal 
cancer. However, there was a new onset LUL consolidation. Given 
her improving clinical picture with COPD treatment and diuresis, 
as well as her lack of fever, white count, and non-toxic 
appearance it was thought that she was unlikely to have a 
pneumonia and antibiotics were held. Upon discharge she will 
need to have her prednisone tapered. She will need 3 more days 
of 60mg prednisone daily until ___, 40mg of prednisone 
daily from ___, and finally her baseline dose of 20mg 
daily. She will also need to have her neublizer treatments 
downtitrated. Upon discharge she is receiving Q6H albuterol and 
ipratropium nebs, which can be reduced to PRNs when clinically 
appropriate.      

# Acute systolic CHF: Upon admission the patient had 1+ edema 
bilaterally, which she reported was above her baseline. Her BNP 
was almost 7000 (almost 6 times over only prior BNP). Her Last 
ECHO demonstrated LVEF of 50% with Moderate PA systolic 
hypertension. Given these findings it was thought that some 
degree of CHF was contributing to her shortness of breath. She 
was given lasix at twice her home dose for 2 days until her Na 
began to drop and her Cr began to rise. Lasix was then held for 
renal protection. Her symptoms improved with diuresis. Upon 
discharge her lasix was stopped.  She should resume lasix 20mg 
PO if her weight is higher than 87kg. 

# h/o afib: The patient had a history of afib but was in NSR 
upon admission. She was continued on Amiodarone and metoprolol 
for rhythm and rate control, and remained in NSR throughout her 
hospital course. She was continued on plavix for a CHADS2 of 1 
and allergy to aspirin.  

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES:
- Patient will need to have toe amputations with vascular 
surgery. An appointment should be scheduled for 2 weeks after 
discharge, and she has been instructed to call to make this 
appointment.
- Patient will need a steroid taper. 60mg prednisone daily until 
___. 40mg prednisone daily from ___, 
thereafter 20mg daily. 
- She will also need her lasix dose titrated to symptoms.   
- Patient will need to follow up with a pulmonologist. An 
appointment has been made. 
- Patient will need to follow up with her oncologist in 6 months 
for her tracheal cancer with repeat imaging. An appointment has 
been made.

INDICATION:  ___ female with shortness of breath and wheezing.

COMPARISON:  ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Single frontal chest radiograph was obtained portably with the
patient in an upright position.

FINDINGS:  Lung volumes are low but improved compared to prior.  Note is made
of an accessory fissure; elevated right hemidiaphragm persists.  No focal
consolidation or pneumothorax is detected on this view.  Right pleural
effusion has improved.  Heart size is enlarged and unchanged.  The aorta is
calcified and tortuous.  There has been interval removal of right PICC and
left hemodialysis catheter.  No pulmonary edema is detected.  Right humeral
replacement hardware is partially imaged.

IMPRESSION:  Cardiomegaly and low lung volumes. Improved aeration and dec'd
right pleural effusion compared to prior.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with history of tracheal cancer status post
chemoradiation, to evaluate for recurrence.

COMPARISON:  None available.

TECHNIQUE:  Multidetector CT imaging of the neck was obtained without
intravenous contrast.  The intravenous contrast was deferred due to the
patient's elevated creatinine.  Sagittal and coronal reformations were
performed and reviewed.

FINDINGS:  The pharyngeal and laryngeal air columns are normal, without
evidence of mass or narrowing.  No significant cervical lymphadenopathy is
seen.  The prevertebral soft tissues are normal.  Thyroid gland, parotid and
submandibular salivary glands are normal.  The imaged portion of the brain
appears unremarkable.  The imaged paranasal sinuses are clear.   The vascular
structures in the neck are unremarkable in this non-contrast examination.

The imaged portion of the upper chest demonstrates consolidation with air
bronchogram in the superior segment of the right lower lobe in this patient
status post right upper lobectomy. Consolidation and ground-glass opacities in
the left upper lobe partially imaged and are better assessed in the concurrent
chest CT.

No bone lesions suspicious for infection or malignancy are detected.  Moderate
degenerative changes are seen in the cervical spine, with reversal of normal
cervical lordosis, centered at C4-C5.  There is significant disc height loss
and endplate irregularity at C4-C5 and C5-C6 levels.

IMPRESSION: No evidence of acute pharyngeal or tracheal abnormality.

NOTE ADDED IN ATTENDING REVIEW: Incidentally noted is medialized,
retropharyngeal course of the both ICAs, left more than right. The findings in
the lung apices, incompletely imaged, appear improved from the study of
___, superimposed on baseline abnormality, likely related to prior
surgery and radiotherapy.

COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY OF THE THORAX

INDICATION:  Tracheal obstruction, brachial cancer, status post chemotherapy,
assessment for tracheal obstruction and potential recurrence.

COMPARISON:  ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Volumetric CT acquisitions over the entire thorax in inspiration,
no administration of intravenous contrast material, multiplanar
reconstructions.

Fistulization of the thoracic inlet is substantially limited by massive
artifacts from metallic shoulder implants.

In the cervical region, the trachea is unchanged and normal.  At the level of
the aortic arch, the trachea is partly collapsed, likely caused by
insufficient inspiration.  However, no peritracheal or paratracheal
abnormalities are noted.  Small tracheal diverticulum.

There is status post right upper lobectomy.  Staples and post-surgical
material are in situ.  This material is surrounded by soft tissue, mainly
located medially to the surgical staples.  This soft tissue structures have
not increased in size and extent.

Massive coronary calcifications.  Mild aortic arch and descending aortal
calcifications.  No incidental thyroid findings.  No mediastinal or hilar
lymphadenopathy.  No subcarinal lymphadenopathy.  No enlarged lymph nodes
along the esophagus and the descending aorta.

Known right dystrophic breast calcifications, status post right breast
surgery.

In the interval, the extent of the right pleural effusion has decreased.  Also
decreased are the previously extensive left and right parenchymal opacities. 
These opacities are more subtle, less solid, and currently predominating in
the upper lobes (4, 55).  Although the examination 
technique is suboptimal, the airways appear patent, with the exception of some
mucus plugging in the region of the right hilus.

Sagittal reconstructions show moderate degenerative vertebral disease, but no
evidence of osteolytic lesions.  No sternal lesions, no osteodestructive rib
lesions.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Improvement of the pre-existing right pleural effusion, improvement of the
parenchymal opacities that are much more loose, less solid and less extensive
than on the previous images.  On the current examination, the lesions are
predominant in the right and left upper lobes.
2.  Unchanged mild increase in soft tissue material around the right stump
after right upper lobectomy.  No evidence of increased interval soft tissue.
3.  Mucus plugging, otherwise patent airways.
4.  Extensive calcification, no evidence of hilar or mediastinal
lymphadenopathy.
